statement: Global age-standardized suicide rate fell 36% 2000-2019 (WHO); GHE values: 12.51 (2000) -> 9.42 (2019) -> 9.13 (2021).
2000-2019 rates fell in five WHO regions (17% E. Mediterranean to 47% Europe, 49% W. Pacific) but 'in the Americas Region, rates increased by 17%' (WHO).
From adjusted 23/100k in 1995-99 (~287,000 deaths/yr) to WHO GHE 8.75 in 2019; 1987-2020 registration analysis: urban ASR down ~66%, rural ~81%; historical female excess reversed after 2005.
topic: China — one of the world's largest declines

statement: WHO-estimated rate fell 53.06 (2000) -> 24.47 (2019) -> 21.37 (2021); 2006 alcohol policy attributed 'an immediate and permanent reduction of about 9%' in male suicide mortality (~4,000 male lives/yr), no detected female effect (AJPH 2013).
topic: Russia — steep decline from world-leading levels

statement: Undetermined-intent deaths declined far more slowly than coded suicides; true mortality likely exceeds Rosstat by ~60% (M) / >2x (F) — part of the recorded decline is coding migration, not fewer deaths.

NCRB record 170,924 (2022; 12.4/lakh, up from 9.9 in 2017) — highest in 56 yrs of ADSI — while WHO GHE modeled rates declined (15.93 in 2000 -> 12.56 in 2021). Part of the recorded rise plausibly reflects improving reporting against a large historical undercount.
topic: India — rising recorded counts vs flat-declining modeled rate

statement: Peer-reviewed meta-analysis: 17.9% of suicides missing from official statistics worldwide — implying >1 million actual deaths/yr vs WHO's ~727,000 — concentrated in LMICs incl. India and China (34.9%).

US age-adjusted incidence (all sites) stable 2013-2022 (~445.8/100k), but aggregate masks divergence: rising in women and several sites (breast, prostate, pancreas, liver in women, melanoma, oral cavity, uterine corpus) while falling/stable in others.
US cancer mortality falling, not rising: death rate down 34% from 1991 peak through 2023 (~4.8M deaths averted), −1.5%/yr 2014-2023, 5-yr relative survival 70%.
Globally, new cancer cases under 50 rose 79% 1990-2019 (3.26M in 2019) while early-onset deaths rose only 28% — incidence rising much faster than mortality.
US cancer incidence in women <50 now 82% higher than men <50 (up from 51% in 2002); colorectal incidence rising ~3%/yr ages 20-49 while falling 2.5%/yr in 65+.

Multiple independent US measures show depression rising over the last decade: PHQ-8 symptoms 18.5% (2019) → 21.4% (2022) per NCHS/NHIS; Gallup ever-diagnosed 20.6% (2017) → 29.0% (2023); steepest among 18-29s and women.
Counterpoint: 2024 NSDUH shows adolescent past-year MDE fell 18.1% (2023) → 15.4% (2024); adult SMI roughly flat (5.7% → 5.6%) — recent official data do not show a continuing monotonic rise.

US adult anxiety symptoms (GAD-7) rose 15.6% (2019) → 18.2% (2022), ages 18-29 19.5% → 26.6% (NCHS/NHIS); WHO estimated a 25% global increase in anxiety and depression in the first pandemic year; anxiety disorders 359M people (4.4%) in 2021.

US overdose deaths peaked at 107,941 (2022, rate 32.6), fell to 105,007 (2023) and 79,384 (2024, −26.2%, largest one-year decline of 2014-2024), provisional 2025 ~69,973 (−14%, third consecutive annual decline). A major documented counterpoint to a worsening-overdose narrative.

US life expectancy flat 2014-2019 (78.9→78.8), fell to 77.0 (2020) and 76.4 (2021), recovered to 77.5 (2022), 78.4 (2023), 79.0 (2024) — above pre-pandemic. Still trails peer average (82.7 in 2024; 3.7-yr gap), a divergence that widened through the 2010s and pandemic and narrowed slightly 2023-2024.

Consensus: point prevalence low and stable — GBD 2016 global age-standardised 0.28% (UI 0.24-0.31), age-specific prevalence 'largely consistent over time and across countries'; case growth (13.1m 1990 -> 20.9m 2016) driven by population growth/ageing.
GBD 2021: prevalent cases +70.1% (13.62m -> 23.18m 1990-2021) but age-standardised prevalence 'relatively stable', incidence slightly declining (EAPC -0.04) — no epidemic of new disease.
NIMH: US prevalence of schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders 0.25%-0.64%; international 0.33%-0.75% — consistent with the ~0.3-0.7% consensus band.

Denmark national registry 2000-2018: diagnosed schizophrenia incidence did NOT rise (1.8 -> 1.6 per 10,000); schizotypal diagnoses nearly doubled — shifts in diagnostic practice within the spectrum, not rising schizophrenia.

Antipsychotic items in England rose 146% (4.71m 1998 -> 11.62m 2022; +111% per capita) 'despite stable estimated prevalence of psychotic disorders' — prescribing volume and diagnosis prevalence have decoupled.
NHSBSA: antipsychotic items 11.0m (2015/16) -> 13.2m (2021/22, +19.7%) -> 13.9m items / 873,000 patients (2024/25); recent year-on-year growth under 1% (Q3 2024/25).

Hong Kong 11-year population study of 62,607 schizophrenia-spectrum patients (2011-2021, joinpoint regression; J Psychiatr Res 2025, PMID 39961232, DOI 10.1016/j.jpsychires.2025.02.017) documents territory-wide utilization trends. Antidepressant items rose every year on record: 61.9m (2015/16) -> 83.4m (2021/22) -> 92.6m (2024/25), 8.89m patients — ~50% volume increase in nine years.

US antidepressant dispensing to adolescents/young adults (IQVIA ~92% of pharmacies, 2016-2022) rose 63.5% faster after March 2020 than pre-pandemic trend — +130% among female adolescents — while male adolescent dispensing declined (Chua et al., Pediatrics 2024).
US stimulant prescriptions +60% 2012-2023 (50.4m -> 80.8m), accelerating after 2020; women +92% vs men +36%; ages 31-40 +240% (DEA/IQVIA, Nov 2024).
Commercially insured 5-64 with >=1 stimulant fill: 3.6% (2016) -> 4.1% (2021), with 2020->2021 jumps ~14-19% among adult women and men 25-44 (CDC MMWR 2023).
CNS stimulant/ADHD items in England more than doubled 1.31m (2015/16) -> 3.38m (2024/25); adults prescribed rose 24.3% in one year to 190,000.

Benzodiazepines run counter: England hypnotic/anxiolytic items FELL 12% (15.9m 2015/16 -> 14.0m 2021/22; 13.4m 2024/25); US adults 65+ fell 14.1 -> 11.5 per 100 (2015-2024), declining pre-pandemic then plateauing.

US adult antipsychotic use rose 1.9% (2006) -> 3.0% (2023) of adults — several times the ~0.3-0.6% schizophrenia prevalence, confirming most volume is prescribed for other conditions; youth use slightly declined (1.3% -> 1.1%).

US overdose deaths rose from 16,849 in 1999 (rate 6.1) to 107,941 in 2022 (rate 32.6) — a 541% increase in the count over twenty-three years, with the steepest acceleration after 2013 and the largest single-year rise in 2020 (+30.0%). The post-2022 decline runs down from that peak, not from the pre-2000 baseline: provisional 2025 (69,973) is still about four times the 1999 count.
